PullRequest.Title: sessions: align list row hover feedback
PullRequest.Body:
Aligns hover feedback across Sessions list rows so sessions, workspace folders, custom groups, shortcuts, and show-more rows use the same full-width square background.

Preserves the intended content spacing for section labels and show-more separators, and reserves the row-spacing height for shortcut entries. Adds regression coverage for row classes, geometry, and padding.

Validation:
- `npm run compile`
- `npm run hygiene`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts` (145 passing)
- Live Agents window verification of hover color, width, radius, margins, and content padding

Scenarios.Scenario: Hovering, focusing, or selecting session, workspace-folder, custom-group, shortcut, and show-more rows in the Sessions list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pointer/focus state changes trigger browser selector matching and repaint for the affected visible virtual-list row. The diff removes inset margin/radius styling and transparent-background overrides and adds a simple active-shortcut hover override; it adds no synchronous geometry reads or JavaScript work to this runtime path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible virtualized rows and interaction events; only the affected hovered/focused/selected row changes state per event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single browser UI-thread style/repaint pass; interaction affects one hovered/focused row at a time, while selection state is bounded by the list's visible rendered rows.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The virtualized tree continues to reuse rendered row templates. CSS state matching has no application cache, and the diff does not alter cold/warm data-loading behavior or cache keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the only changed runtime cost is bounded CSS style/paint work, based on the changed selectors and renderer class application path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact repaint cost varies by viewport and platform, but the changed painted area is one row and the selectors are shallow class/state selectors; no realistic scaling mechanism establishes a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The styling changes alter row feedback geometry and paint, but do not add forced layout, repeated collection-wide work, or an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Laying out, resizing, and scrolling the Sessions virtual tree with shortcut sections and row spacing enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tree calls SessionsTreeDelegate.getHeight for list elements to calculate virtual row positions. Shortcut sections now execute two string equality checks and add the existing two-pixel inset gap; all operations are constant-time and complete synchronously before layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total tree elements during height calculation, with effective changed cardinality limited to the Automations and Customizations section rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on the browser UI thread by the virtual tree; rendered DOM remains bounded to the viewport by virtualization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No data cache behavior changes. Existing virtual-list template reuse remains intact, and the shortcut classification has no miss/retry or invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the delegate implementation: isShortcutSection is two direct identifier comparisons, and withInsetRowSpacing is one conditional numeric addition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The total item count varies by session history, but the added work is O(1) per section and applies only to the small fixed set of shortcut sections, not every session row.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra classification and arithmetic are negligible and do not change algorithmic complexity or trigger browser layout reads.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating and recycling custom-group rows in the virtual Sessions list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When a group-row template is created, AbstractTreeRenderer.renderTemplate adds the new static session-list-section-row class before rendering its DOM; recycled rows retain the class without repeated per-frame work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of custom-group DOM templates created, effectively bounded by visible rows plus the tree's reusable template pool.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous template creation on the UI thread, bounded by the number of visible/recycled virtual-list templates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The list's existing template recycling is unchanged; warm templates avoid recreation, and no application cache or negative-cache state is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the traced AbstractTreeRenderer rowClassName plumbing and SessionGroupRenderer declaration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of custom groups can vary, but only viewport-visible templates are materialized and the changed operation is one classList.add per template creation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. A single template-time class insertion and associated ordinary CSS matching do not establish meaningful CPU, layout, rendering, or memory growth.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and every diff page. Traced virtual-row height calculation, renderer class plumbing, CSS hover/focus behavior, template recycling, and external-boundary reachability. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression was found.
